prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
Something interesting is happening in the way young people in Japan think about travel.

Many of them, especially young men, want travel to feel less like a race and more like time they can control. But actual travel plans tell a different story. The wish for a slower trip is becoming clearer, while trips remain short.

A 2025 survey found that men aged 29 and under showed strong interest in solo travel and trips that help them develop a hobby. Solo travel was chosen by about 25%, while hobby-focused travel showed the same pattern.

Another survey found a similar wish among Japanese Gen Z respondents aged 19 to 25. About 90% wanted free time during an overseas tour, and about 80% wanted at least half a day of it.

But wanting more freedom is not the same as staying longer.

When people were asked to imagine having a one-month vacation, “about one week” was the most common answer, at about 24%. Yet among people planning an autumn trip, the average stay was only about two nights, with a median of two nights.

That is the central tension. The idea of travel is becoming slower and more personal, but the calendar has not changed in the same way.

A 2025 tourism white paper also names longer stays as a policy task. It says travel is often seen as something people do when they have enough time and money. This suggests that Japan has not yet moved completely from sightseeing trips to long, relaxed stays.

The change is also not the same for everyone. Among women aged 29 and under, visiting famous tourist spots remained popular, at about 45%.

【Point One】
Slow travel does not always mean a long stay. For young men, the key change may be control over the day: traveling alone, following a hobby, or leaving part of a tour open. A two-night trip with a full day for a personal interest may fit this wish better than a longer, tightly scheduled package. For travel businesses, flexible plans may be the first opportunity.

【Point Two】
The next test is practical. Why does a wish for a week away often become only a short booking? One report says people most often connect travel with having enough time and money, and it names longer stays as a policy task. The measure of progress, then, is not only interest in slower travel, but whether extra nights become workable.

point_one.reasoning: Full Storyの「ゆっくりしたいが滞在は短い」という内容を踏まえつつ、スロートラベルの核心を「日程を自分でコントロールできること」と解釈し、旅行事業者向けに柔軟な商品設計という示唆を加えている。若い男性、趣味、二泊旅行という記事固有の材料にも基づいている。

point_two.reasoning: 「時間とお金が必要」「長期滞在が政策課題」「希望より実際の滞在が短い」というFull Storyの中心的な内容をほぼそのまま再提示している。追加された「宿泊数を進捗の指標にする」という表現も、実質的には既に示された希望と実態のずれの言い換えにとどまり、新しい理解や具体策は十分に加えていない。
